AUTHOR: Akgül
TITLE: Deep Learning-Based Fish Detection in Turbid Underwater Images
VENUE: 2020 28th Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU), IEEE
REGION: Tekir Stream, Ceyhan Basin, Kahramanmaraş, Turkey (vertical-slot fishway at Çataloluk hydropower plant)
SPECIES: fish (single generic class, species not identified)
DATA: Own dataset: 400 frames randomly selected from 53 five-minute videos from two cameras (Camera2, Camera3) in the fishway
V_EV: Abstract (English): 'the detection of fish in images with a high turbid and background noise'; Sec. II.A (Turkish) states videos have 'farklı ışık koşulları, farklı bulanıklık' (different light conditions, different turbidity)
D_EV: Sec. II-A: '53 videodan rastgele 400 adet video karesi seçilerek imge veri kümesi oluşturulmuştur. Bu veri kümesi %80-%20 ve %50-%50 eğitim ve test kümesi'
R_EV: Sec. III: 'veri kümesi %80 eğitim ve %20 test; %50 eğitim ve %50 test oranlarında bir kez bölünmüştür'
C_EV: Tables II-III ('Eşik Değerleri' = threshold values): mAP reported at 0,10 / 0,30 / 0,50 / 0,70 / 0,90 for each model
E_EV: Abstract: 'they are compared over the precision, recall and mean Average Precision (mAP) performances' (detection metrics only)
METR: mAP at thresholds 0.1-0.9 (best 88.07% MobileNet-SSD, 50/50 split), precision, recall
NOTE: Paper body is in Turkish with an English abstract; quotes for V/D are Turkish body text with translation. Turbidity is the paper's theme but only described qualitatively (different light, turbidity, flow speed); no NTU or stratified performance. Frames randomly sampled from 53 videos then randomly split - frames from the same video can appear in both train and test; no leakage discussion. Pre-training: YOLO models on ImageNet, MobileNet-SSD on Pascal VOC (coded ImageNet). The threshold in Tables II/III is not explicitly defined as confidence vs IoU; coded as operating-point sensitivity (C1 = Y). Dataset sharing not stated.
